RQ1.rationale: The paper gives a general CubeSat mission/system reference model using logical architecture and reusable SysML artifacts, but it does not model EPS behavior in detail.

RQ2.rationale: It claims reuse, completeness, economies of scale, mission success, and community integration benefits from CSRM use, but these are system-level and not derived from EPS modeling or quantified reliability evidence.

RQ3.rationale: The CSRM includes verification/validation activity elements and requirements traceability before physical development, but no EPS-specific verification procedure or test result is reported.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper explicitly builds on earlier CSRM work on behaviors, V&V, technical measures, and CSRM development cited as references [1]-[6]. This extraction uses only the 2021 paper text and treats it as a mission-engineering extension roadmap rather than a new EPS case study.

RQ1: The CSRM models CubeSat missions through a reusable SysML-compliant logical space-ground architecture rather than a mission-specific physical design.
Generality is achieved by keeping stakeholders, technical measures, behaviors, and requirements unpopulated until a mission team tailors the model.
Power availability, energy collection, and energy consumption appear only as trade-study factors, not as a detailed EPS model.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include completeness, economies of scale, reuse, component sharing, mission success, and a unifying environment for universities.
Reliability is not explicitly claimed or measured, and reproducibility/integrability outcomes are system-level rather than EPS-derived.
Evidence consists mainly of assertions, reported professional vetting, and references to prior demonstrations, without metrics or baseline comparison in this paper.
RQ3: The CSRM includes model elements and trace relationships for requirements, technical measures, validation activities, and verification activities before physical development.
The paper does not report an EPS-specific verification procedure, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop setup, integration test, or physical test result.
Mission-level V&V support for the extended Mission Engineering use case remains to be evaluated.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: The CSRM is based on Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) principles, is System Modeling Language (SysML) compliant, is hosted in a graphical modeling tool, and is intended to foster completeness and economies of scale associated with reusability.
The CSRM provides a CubeSat logical space-ground architecture.
The logical components are abstractions of the physical components that perform the system functionality without imposing implementation constraints.
The CSRM is a repository for systems engineering artifacts. However, it is not pre-populated with specific stakeholders, technical measures, behaviors, and requirements.

The CSRM provides for defining and tracing requirements from stakeholders, to behaviors, with technical measures assigned to subsystems and components to be certified through validation and verification activities.
A mission-specific CubeSat team downloads the CSRM specification and files from OMG for import it into their own graphical modeling tool.
The trade studies are based on the modeling of collecting mission observations, storage, downlink, energy collection, and energy consumption.
extending it beyond that point to incorporate a dynamic, analytical capability to assess overall mission performance would be challenging and an area that would require much further research.

As stated previously and shown in Figure 1, the current CSRM provides support for verification and validation activities. The level to which that supports Mission Engineering activities would have to be evaluated.
Stage 3 will consist of carrying out and reporting on implementation evaluations. Updating the OMG CSRM specification and files requires OMG and INCOSE approval.

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: Code this study as a system-level CubeSat MBSE reference-model and mission-engineering roadmap paper. It overlaps with earlier Kaslow CSRM papers but, under the silo rules, only the 2021 text supports this extraction. Do not treat references to prior demonstrations as direct EPS evidence.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The full markdown was available and the paper clearly describes CSRM scope, artifacts, and limitations. Confidence is lower only for claimed outcomes because the paper itself provides limited empirical evidence.
